spots.name: Dome of the Rock

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Dome of the Rock is an octagonal Islamic shrine at the center of the Al-Aqsa mosque compound on the Temple Mount in the Old City of Jerusalem.

spots.name: Al-Aqsa Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Aqsa Mosque, also known as the Qibli Mosque, is the main congregational mosque or prayer hall in the Al-Aqsa mosque compound in the Old City of Jerusalem.

names.ja: アル＝アクサー・モスク

spots.name: Temple Mount

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Temple Mount or al-Haram al-Sharif is an elevated plateau in the Old City of Jerusalem that comprises the Islamic religious compound known as al-Aqsa, which includes the al-Aqsa Mosque and the Dome of the Rock.

spots.name: Calvary
spots.summary: Calvary or Golgotha, derived from Golgolta, was a site immediately outside Roman Jerusalem's walls where, according to Christianity's four canonical gospels, Jesus was crucified.

spots.name: Church of the Holy Sepulchre
spots.summary: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre, also known as the Church of the Resurrection, is a fourth-century church in the Christian Quarter of the Old City of Jerusalem.

spots.name: Western Wall
spots.summary: The Western Wall is an ancient retaining wall of the built-up hill known to Jews and Christians as the Temple Mount of Jerusalem.

spots.name: Second Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Second Temple was the temple in Jerusalem that replaced Solomon's Temple, which was destroyed during the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem in 587 BCE.

spots.name: Old City of Jerusalem
spots.summary: The Old City of Jerusalem is a 0.9-square-kilometre (0.35 sq mi) walled area in East Jerusalem.

spots.name: Temple in Jerusalem

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Temple in Jerusalem, or alternatively the Holy Temple, refers to the two religious structures that served as the central places of worship for Israelites and Jews on the Temple Mount in the Old City of Jerusalem.

photo.author: Sarah Murray from South Bend, IN, USA

spots.name: Gethsemane
spots.summary: Gethsemane is a garden as well as a courtyard at the foot of the Mount of Olives in East Jerusalem, where, according to the four Gospels of the New Testament, Jesus Christ underwent the Agony in the Garden and was arrested before his crucifixion. The garden is a place of great resonance in Christianity.

spots.name: Mount Zion
spots.summary: Mount Zion is a hill in Jerusalem located just outside the walls of the Old City to the south. The term Mount Zion has been used in the Hebrew Bible first for the City of David and later for the Temple Mount, but its meaning has shifted and it is now used as the name of ancient Jerusalem's Western Hill.

spots.name: Tower of David
spots.summary: The Tower of David, also known as the Citadel, is an ancient citadel and contemporary museum, located near the Jaffa Gate entrance to the Old City of Jerusalem.

spots.name: Mount of Olives
spots.summary: The Mount of Olives or Mount Olivet is a mountain ridge in East Jerusalem, east of and adjacent to Jerusalem's Old City. It is named for the olive groves that once covered its slopes. The southern part of the mount was the Silwan necropolis, attributed to the elite of the ancient Kingdom of Judah.

spots.name: Al-Aqsa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al-Aqsa, also known as the Haram al-Sharif, is the Islamic religious compound that encompasses the plateau of the Temple Mount, in the Old City of Jerusalem.

spots.name: Church of the Nativity

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Nativity, or Basilica of the Nativity, is a basilica located in Bethlehem, West Bank, Palestine. The grotto holds a prominent religious significance to Christians of various denominations as the birthplace of Jesus.

names.fr: Basilique de la Nativité de Bethléem

spots.name: Israel Museum
spots.summary: The Israel Museum is an art and archaeology museum in Jerusalem. It was established in 1965 as Israel's largest and foremost cultural institution, and an encyclopedic museum.

photo.author: Original uploader was אסף.צ at he.wikipedia

spots.name: Church of Mary Magdalene

hours.note: Closed Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Church of Mary Magdalene is an Eastern Orthodox Christian church located on the Mount of Olives, directly across the Kidron Valley and near the Garden of Gethsemane in Jerusalem.

names.ja: マグダラのマリア教会

spots.name: Temple Institute

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Temple Institute, known in Hebrew as Machon HaMikdash, is an organization in Israel focusing on establishing the Third Temple.

spots.name: Well of Souls
spots.summary: The Well of Souls is a partly natural, partly man-made cave located inside the Foundation Stone under the Dome of the Rock shrine on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem.

spots.name: Tomb of the Virgin Mary
spots.summary: Church of the Sepulchre of Saint Mary, also Tomb of the Virgin Mary or the Church of the Assumption, is a Christian church built around an ancient Judean rock-cut tomb in the Kidron Valley – at the foot of Mount of Olives, in East Jerusalem – believed by Christians to be the burial place of Mary, the mother of Jesus.

spots.name: Gehenna
spots.summary: Gehenna or Gehinnom is a Biblical toponym that has acquired various theological connotations, including as a place of divine punishment, in Jewish eschatology.

spots.name: Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Jerusalem
spots.summary: The Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Jerusalem, also known as the Greek Orthodox Church of Jerusalem, is an autocephalous Eastern Orthodox church in full communion with the other Eastern Orthodox churches.

names.ja: エルサレムのギリシャ正教会
names.zh: 耶路撒冷希腊东正教教会

spots.name: City of David

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The City of David, known locally mostly in Arabic as Wadi Hilweh, is the name given to an archaeological site considered by most scholars to be the original settlement core of Jerusalem during the Bronze and Iron Ages.

spots.name: Cenacle
spots.summary: The Cenacle, also known as the Upper Room, is a room in Mount Zion in Jerusalem, just outside the Old City walls, traditionally held to be the site of the Last Supper, the final meal that, in the Gospel accounts, Jesus held with the apostles.

spots.name: Jaffa Gate
spots.summary: Jaffa Gate is one of the seven main open gates of the Old City of Jerusalem.

spots.name: Walls of Jerusalem
spots.summary: The Walls of Jerusalem surround the Old City of Jerusalem. In 1535, when Jerusalem was part of the Ottoman Empire, Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent ordered the ruined city walls to be rebuilt. The walls were constructed between 1537 and 1541. The walls are visible on most old maps of Jerusalem over the last 500 years.

spots.name: Jewish Quarter
spots.summary: The Jewish Quarter is one of the four traditional quarters of the Old City of Jerusalem.

names.fr: Quartier juif de la vieille ville de Jérusalem
names.es: Barrio judío de la ciudad vieja de Jerusalén

photo.author: Ricardo Tulio Gandelman from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

spots.name: Yad Vashem

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: Yad Vashem is Israel's official memorial institution to the victims of the Holocaust, known in Hebrew as the Shoah (שואה).

names.zh: 以色列犹太大屠杀纪念馆

photo.author: Hagai Agmon-Snir حچاي اچمون-سنير חגי אגמון-שניר

spots.name: Church of the Redeemer, Jerusalem

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Lutheran Church of the Redeemer is an Lutheran-Protestant church in the Old City of Jerusalem. It is the property of the Protestant Jerusalem Foundation, one of the three foundations of the Protestant Church in Germany (EKD) in the Holy Land.

spots.name: Hurva Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hurva Synagogue, also known as Hurvat Rabbi Yehudah he-Hasid, is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located in the Jewish Quarter of the Old City of Jerusalem.

photo.author: Daniel.baranek 19:17, 21 February 2007 (UTC) (Original uploader was Chesdovi at

spots.name: Mosque of Omar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mosque of Omar is a mosque, located inside the Old City of Jerusalem. Situated opposite the southern courtyard of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, in the Muristan area of the Christian Quarter, the mosque is not open to tourists, and can be accessed only for praying. The mosque was completed during the Ayyubid era.

spots.name: Rachel's Tomb
spots.summary: Rachel's Tomb is a site revered as the burial place of the Biblical matriarch Rachel. The site is also referred to as the Bilal bin Rabah mosque. The tomb is held in esteem by Jews, Christians, and Muslims.

spots.name: Lions' Gate
spots.summary: Lions' Gate, also St Stephen's Gate, is one of the seven open Gates of the Old City of Jerusalem. It leads into the Muslim Quarter of the Old City.

spots.name: Pool of Bethesda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Pool of Bethesda is referred to in John's Gospel in the Christian New Testament, in an account of Jesus healing a paralyzed man at a pool of water in Jerusalem, described as being near the Sheep Gate and surrounded by five covered colonnades or porticoes. It is also referred to as Bethzatha.

spots.name: Mount Herzl
spots.summary: Mount Herzl, also known as Mount of Remembrance, is the site of Israel's national cemetery and other memorial and educational facilities, found on the west side of Jerusalem beside the Jerusalem Forest.

photo.author: Hagai Agmon-Snir حچاي اچمون-سنير חגי אגמון-שניר

spots.name: Mount Scopus
spots.summary: Mount Scopus is a mountain located in Jerusalem with an elevation of 826 meters (2,710 ft) above sea level.

photo.author: Hagai Agmon-Snir حچاي اچمون-سنير חגי אגמון-שניר

spots.name: Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem
spots.summary: The Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem is the Latin Catholic ecclesiastical patriarchate in Jerusalem, officially seated in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.

names.zh: 天主教耶路撒冷宗主教區

spots.name: Cathedral of Saint James, Jerusalem
spots.summary: The Cathedral of Saint James is a 12th-century Armenian church in the Armenian Quarter of Jerusalem, near the quarter's entry Zion Gate. The cathedral is dedicated to two of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus: James, son of Zebedee and James the brother of Jesus. It is located near the Church of the Holy Archangels.

spots.name: Dormition Abbey

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: Abbey of the Dormition is a Catholic abbey belonging to the Benedictine Order in Jerusalem, on Mount Zion, just outside the walls of the Old City near the Zion Gate. The Abbey is said to mark the spot where Mary, mother of Jesus, ended her worldly existence.

names.fr: Abbaye de la Dormition de Jérusalem

spots.name: Damascus Gate
spots.summary: The Damascus Gate is one of the main Gates of the Old City of Jerusalem.

spots.name: Golden Gate
spots.summary: The Golden Gate or Gate of Mercy is the only eastern gate of the Temple Mount, and one of only two Gates of the Old City of Jerusalem that used to offer access into the city from the East side.

spots.name: Akeldama
spots.summary: Akeldama is the Aramaic name for a place in Jerusalem associated with Judas Iscariot, one of the original twelve apostles of Jesus.

spots.name: King David Hotel
spots.summary: The King David Hotel is a 5-star hotel in Jerusalem and a member of The Leading Hotels of the World. Opened in 1931, it was built with locally quarried pink limestone and was founded by Ezra Mosseri, a wealthy Egyptian Jewish banker.

spots.name: Garden Tomb

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Garden Tomb is an ancient rock-cut tomb surrounded by a garden, right outside the walls of ancient Jerusalem, that functions as a site of Christian pilgrimage attracting hundreds of thousands of annual visitors, especially Evangelicals and other Protestants, as some Protestant Christians consider it to be the empty tomb where Jesus of Nazareth resurrected.

spots.name: Church of the Pater Noster

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Church of the Pater Noster is a Catholic church located on the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem. It is part of a Carmelite monastery of cloistered nuns, also known as the Sanctuary of the Eleona. The Church of the Pater Noster stands next to the ruins of the 4th-century Late Roman/Early Byzantine Church of Eleona.

spots.name: Aelia Capitolina

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Aelia Capitolina was a Roman colony founded during the Roman emperor Hadrian's visit to Judaea in 129/130 CE. It was founded on the ruins of Jerusalem, which had been almost totally razed after the siege of 70 CE.

names.ja: アエリア・カピトリナ

spots.name: Dome of the Chain

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Dome of the Chain is an Islamic free-standing domed building located adjacently east of the Dome of the Rock in the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in the Old City of Jerusalem. It is one of many small buildings that can be found scattered around the Al-Aqsa Mosque.

spots.name: Shrine of the Book

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Shrine of the Book is a wing of the Israel Museum in the Givat Ram neighborhood of Jerusalem that houses the Dead Sea Scrolls and the Aleppo Codex, among other texts.

photo.author: Xavier Gillet, Bordeaux, France (xavier33300 on flickr)

spots.name: Saint Anne's Church

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Church of Saint Anne is a French Catholic church and part of the French national domain in the Holy Land located in the Muslim Quarter of the Old City of Jerusalem, near the start of the Via Dolorosa, next to the Lions' Gate. The site is also known as al-Madrasa as-Salahiyya.

spots.name: Herod's Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Herod's Palace at Jerusalem was built in the last quarter of the 1st century BC by King Herod the Great of Judea from 37 BC to 4 BC. It was the second most important building in Jerusalem, after the Temple itself; in Herod's day and was situated at the northwestern wall of the Upper City of Jerusalem.

spots.name: Antonia Fortress

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Antonia Fortress was a citadel built by Herod the Great and named for Herod's patron Mark Antony, as a fortress whose chief function was to protect the Second Temple.

spots.name: Western Wall Plaza
spots.summary: The Western Wall Plaza is a large public square situated adjacent to the Western Wall in the Jewish Quarter of the Old City of Jerusalem, Israel. It was formed in 1967 as a result of the razing of the Mughrabi Quarter neighborhood at the very end of the Six-Day War.

photo.author: Sustructu stitched by Marku1988 This image was created with Hugin.

spots.name: Dung Gate

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: The Dung Gate, also known as Bab al-Maghariba, Mughrabi Gate, Moroccan Gate or Silwan Gate, is one of the Gates of the Old City of Jerusalem.

spots.name: David's Tomb

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat

spots.summary: David's Tomb is a site that, according to an early medieval tradition, is associated with the burial of the biblical king David. During the Ottoman and British Mandate periods, Maqam Al-Nabi Daoud served one of Jerusalem prime Islamic shrines.

spots.name: Tiferet Yisrael Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Tiferet Yisrael Synagogue, most often spelled Tiferet Israel, also known as the Nisan Bak Shul, after its co-founder, Nisan Bak is a former prominent Hasidic Jewish congregation and synagogue, located in the Jewish Quarter of the Old City of Jerusalem.

spots.name: Zion Gate
spots.summary: Zion Gate, also known in Arabic as Bab Sahyun or Bab Harat al-Yahud, is one of the seven historic Gates of the Old City of Jerusalem.

spots.name: Mahane Yehuda Market

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: Mahane Yehuda Market سوق محاني يهودا), often referred to as "The Shuk", is a marketplace in Jerusalem.

names.ja: マハネ・イェフダ市場

spots.name: Ophel
spots.summary: Ophel is the Hebrew biblical term for an elevated part of a settlement or city, higher than its surroundings, probably meaning a fortified hill or risen area. In the Hebrew Bible, the Ophel refers to two cities: Jerusalem and Samaria.

spots.name: Pool of Siloam
spots.summary: The term Pool of Siloam refers to several rock-cut pools located southeast of the walls of the Old City of Jerusalem. The pools were fed by the waters of the Gihon Spring, carried there by the Siloam tunnel.

spots.name: Jaffa Road
spots.summary: Jaffa Road, also called Jaffa Street is one of the longest and oldest major streets in Jerusalem. It crosses the city from east to west, from the Old City walls to downtown Jerusalem, the western portal of Jerusalem and the Jerusalem–Tel Aviv highway. It is lined with shops, businesses, and restaurants.

spots.name: Museum of Underground Prisoners

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The central prison run by British authorities from 1917-1948. Towards the end of that period, many members of underground Jewish militias were incarcerated here, including several who were later executed. Now the site is a museum commemorating the underground movements and their members who went through this prison.

spots.name: A Walk on the Roofs
spots.summary: It is possible to walk above the central souk along the rooftops of the city. Visitors can climb up to the rooftops via a small staircase at the corner of St Mark's Road and Khabad Street. A second set of stairs leads up from Muristan Road and visitors can exit into the courtyard of Khan el-Sultan, which allows exit onto Chain Street. The view from the rooftops offers delightful views of the bustl

spots.name: Jerusalem YMCA

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A West Jerusalem landmark, built in 1933. There is a tower with views of the surroundings. The view is not bad, but less impressive than one might expect (you can see part of the Old City walls, and the top of Dome of the Rock, but little else of note). Going up the tower costs ₪20 - inquire at the main desk and you should be able to go up with little delay. There are reports that unaccompanied in

names.zh: 耶路撒冷基督教青年会

spots.name: Hansen House
spots.summary: This complex was established in 1887 as a walled-off hospital for patients with leprosy. Nowadays, the grounds form a park, while the building (which is quite beautiful, particularly its internal courtyard) hosts art exhibitions and cultural events. There is also a tower with an impressive view.

spots.name: Teddy Park
spots.summary: Named after Teddy Kollek, Jerusalem mayor from 1965-1993, this park is located in the valley just below Jaffa Gate. The highlight is a fountain with 256 water spouts which performs a choreographed water show once every 2 hours (check the schedule before coming); you are encouraged to run through the fountain on a hot day. There is also a constantly running water feature which is good for cooling o

spots.name: City of David and Jerusalem water system

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: To get here, exit the Old City through Dung Gate (by the Kotel), turn left, and then take the first street on your right. The site comprises two archeological findings.

photo.author: Ricardo Tulio Gandelman from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

spots.name: Yemin Moshe
spots.summary: The first neighborhood of Jerusalem to be built outside the Old City. The Mishkenot Sha'ananim housing project and the landmark windmill were finished in 1860; the rest of the neighborhood was built in the 1890s. Nowadays the neighborhood is quaint, beautiful, surrounded by parkland, and with a direct view of the Old City walls. It's a delightful neighborhood to walk around, both during the day an

spots.name: Hebrew Music Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A museum that describes the history of Jewish music across different time periods and cultures.

spots.name: Friends of Zion Museum
spots.summary: This museum brings the stories of non-Jewish help and heroism to the world, who supported Zionism and stood bravely with the Jewish people. Visitors experience the unfolding story as though stepping back in time. Accompanied by a moving original musical score and surround sound, meet the biblical figures, academics, businessmen, and military officials who, through their faith, have forged an everl

spots.name: Italian Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The center of the Italian-origin Jewish community in Jerusalem. In addition to the synagogue, whose ancient wooden decorations were transferred from Italy and reassembled, there is a museum displaying beautiful art and Judaica. Shabbat prayers are held each week; Shabbat morning prayers begin at 08:30 and are often followed by an Italian-style kiddush.

spots.name: Worldwide North Africa Jewish Heritage Center

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An interesting museum about the heritage of Jews from North African countries. You can only visit by advance reservation and as part of a group of 20 or more. Contact them and they might be able to arrange something.

spots.name: Gorny Convent
spots.summary: A Russian Orthodox convent dating to the 19th century

photo.author: Hagai Agmon-Snir حچاي اچمون-سنير חגי אגמון-שניר

spots.name: Amigo Emil
spots.summary: This friendly place, set on a quiet bazaar street at the edge of the Christian Quarter, is a good choice for a Western-style meal and a break from the bustle of the Old City. You can order chicken wings in barbecue sauce; omelets; old-fashioned chicken soup; meat lasagna; boneless, breaded chicken breast stuffed with Israeli feta cheese; a mezze of Arabic appetizers; or grilled meats. There are sp

spots.name: Versavee Bistro Bar & Cafe
spots.summary: A lovely bistro/cafe/bar where you can enjoy and chill, listen to cool music, and watch TV. Soft drinks, beers & beverages, fresh fruit juices, snacks, munchies, full cocktail bar, tobacco & free wifi. Try the local Palestinian beer called Taybeh—only ₪18. One of the nicest and cleanest cafes in the Old City. This small indoor/outdoor cafe/restaurant/bar is a nice spot for lunch, dinner or late ni

spots.name: Agas Vetapuah

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Considered to be among the best Italian restaurants in Jerusalem. The restaurant is owned by Yonatan Ottolenghi, an Italian from Milano, who is often in the restaurant and sells his handmade liqueur in the restaurant. The restaurant serves various Italian dishes such as: pizzas, pastas, lasagnas and antipasti; and its blintzes are famed throughout Jerusalem. OU Kosher.

spots.name: Marvad Haksammim

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: With its large serving sizes this is one of the best places for Yemenite food in the city. Be sure to try the Kuba soup (red, sweet, and spicy with round meat dumplings), Saluf (think large, thick, and crispy burritos), Shakshuka (poached eggs in tomato sauce), and Malawakh (doughy sweet pancake). Entrees are ₪15-40. Kosher.

spots.name: Imbala

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Imbala is a 100% vegan, member-run cooperative that serves food & drinks. It serves as an Israeli/Palestinian/queer/leftist/*-inclusive space that's multigenerational and multilingual. Come have a sandwich, coffee, and browse through their zines or other feminist/queer/marxist/Israeli/Palestinian literature.

spots.name: The Cassette

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: With the electric conduits forming a vine pattern over your head in its crypt-like backroom, this bar screams 'talk to me about philosophy' while experimental music plays in the background. The customers are the sort of people you'd find lounging around in art student's dorm room--in the best way possible.

spots.name: Bein Aza LeBerlin

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: At the corner of Gaza St and Berlin St, with a second branch downtown. A small and friendly place selling hummus and falafel, has excellent Kube soup of different types. Coming here on a Friday afternoon is a truly classic Israeli experience. Kosher.

spots.name: Mike's Place

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Live-music sports bar and grill, with a large international menu including American and Tex-Mex standards. The only branch of the Mike's Place chain that is Kosher. Mike's Place opened in Jerusalem in 1992, and is a landmark of Jerusalem nightlife.

spots.name: Burgers Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A hamburger chain with branches throughout the city (and elsewhere). They have relatively slow and sloppy service and questionable hygiene at busy hours. The food is relatively cheap, about ₪50 for a 150g hamburger, fries and a soft drink. Kosher.

spots.name: The Eucalyptus

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Biblical Israeli cuisine best known for its "shir hashirim (Song of Songs)" tasting menu. There is a view of the David Citadel from the restaurant and the chefs are internationally acclaimed. Reservations recommended. Kosher.

spots.name: Tmol Shilshom

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This cafe/bookstore is the top destination for Jerusalem's literati. In addition to serving food and coffee, there are frequently scheduled cultural events such as lectures and musical performances held while you eat. Kosher.

spots.name: Cafe Kadosh

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Founded in 1967, this cafe is considered to be one of the best in Jerusalem. Serving excellent pastries, eggs and pastas; you will feel like you are in Europe. Reservations are recommended, especially on Fridays. Kosher.

spots.name: Armenian Tavern

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Traditional Armenian food in an atmospheric setting: a Crusader period arched cellar complete with indoor fountain, wooden tables and the ubiquitous hand-painted Armenian tiles. Alcoholic beverages available.

spots.name: Birman

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Musical bistro: live music every night. For art, music & good food lovers. Open daily 19:00 till late hours, Friday 13:00 – Sabbath, closed Saturday.

spots.name: Prague

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An east European bar restaurant offering some great ethnic food together with big amount of draught beers and some exclusive attractions.

spots.name: Ha-Tipa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Small neighborhood pub on the outskirts of the Machaneh Yehuda market. Very cheap alcohol, good music and photo gallery.

spots.name: Sira

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: A manifold and interesting pub. Live DJs every night. Jazz and mellow during the day.
